# Decisions for applying the Fluent / WinUI guidance (current Microsoft guidance, Windows 11)

Owner's rule: where current guidance disagrees with the Windows 7 guide on behaviour, current guidance wins for the Windows form (and Linux takes the Windows form). Apple's forms are untouched. When the Windows form now says the same as the macOS form, merge them: drop both forms, put the shared behaviour in the rule text, set plat false. Remove phrases like "Windows 7 guide; current Fluent guidance could not be fetched" and "Fluent not consulted": Fluent has now been read (except its keyboard pages: keyboard accessibility, keyboard interactions, access keys, keyboard accelerators, focus navigation, visual feedback, which were not in the copy supplied; rules resting on those keep the Windows 7 form and may say so).

Per rule (apply these; for rules not listed, apply the CHANGE/REMOVE/ADD records with your judgment):

- WRD-2: Windows: drop the four-word allowance for toolbar buttons; a toolbar button's label is preferably one word.
- WRD-6: Windows: sentence case for all text, including window and dialog titles and a flow's name; title case nowhere.
- WRD-7: Windows: specific response labels preferred; a message that only needs dismissing has Close; OK, Cancel, Apply only on a properties dialog of one object; Yes and No only where no specific answer is possible, as a pair (the Buttons page still lists them). Remove "OK commits a window that changes settings".
- WRD-14: Windows: a problem message may have the app take responsibility in the active voice with "we" (We couldn't save your file); macOS: no "we". The rule becomes platform-specific (Q-15 settled this way).
- WRD-17: Windows: "select" is the input-neutral verb for buttons and commands as well as list items; "click" is no longer required.
- WRD-19: no colon after a label on any platform (Q-22 settled). The placeholder stays while the field is focused and empty and goes at the first character, returning when emptied, on every platform (so no platform split there). A visible label stays the default; a placeholder alone is allowed where the purpose is obvious from context (search field, toolbar field, a sign-in pair).
- WRD-20, CTL-5: drop the colon after group labels and dependent-control labels.
- WRD-21: Windows: Back in a guided flow is a labelled button beside Next among the bottom buttons.
- WRD-25: keep the rule strict; add that Fluent's own examples show "Loading…" beside a bar, allowed only where the object is obvious from the screen.
- CMD-1: Windows: a menu bar is for apps with many commands in several categories (editing apps, like Notepad); other main windows may use a toolbar (command bar) with a More menu as their command surface. Either way every command is reachable from a visible command surface (menu bar, or toolbar plus its More menu), not only from context menus. macOS unchanged. (Q-1 answered this way.)
- CMD-3, CMD-8, CMD-20, WIN-16, WIN-23: Windows: Settings (named Settings, not Options) is a page in the app's window, applying each change at once, no OK/Cancel/Apply; it is the last item of the navigation sidebar, or the last item of the toolbar's More menu (or on the toolbar); with a menu bar and no sidebar, the last item of Tools. About is a section at the bottom of the Settings page (name, icon, version, links), not a Help menu item. OK/Cancel/Apply remain only for a properties dialog of one object. The settings command may now be a toolbar item. (Q-2 settled: live settings.)
- CMD-10: Windows: an item's context menu holds every command that acts on that item (leaving out what does not apply); common commands (Cut, Copy, Paste, Delete, Rename, Share) come first (Windows 11 shows them as a row of symbols); in a text field's menu, Cut/Copy appear only with a selection and Paste only with clipboard text (left out, not disabled). Remove the Windows 7 order and "stay in, disabled". Floating commands on a text selection fold in here.
- CMD-17: menus hold only commands and options.
- CTL-2: Windows: an on/off setting that applies at once is a switch; a checkbox is for a choice committed later with its form, or for picking several; radio buttons for two to five options (as on macOS), more in a select; drop "radio buttons on guided-flow pages"; a single binary choice is never two radio buttons; a three-valued choice is a radio group, not a mixed checkbox. If the forms now agree, merge.
- CTL-5: a click on a mixed checkbox turns all on, the next all off; no cycle back to the mix on any platform (Q-27 settled). kvit-ui's Check already does this (`check.go:49-51`): update "now" to enforces for that part.
- CTL-8: one rule on every platform: a submit button may stay disabled until required fields are filled, with the required fields marked and the reason shown (Q-30 settled).
- CTL-9: Windows: stepping stops at the limits, the step button that would pass a limit is disabled, the buttons sit beside the field; drop wrap and arrows inside the box (Q-26 settled; KvitStepper already clamps and disables at the ends, `stepper.go:67-68`).
- CTL-10: beyond a few static pages, prefer a navigation sidebar to a tab row; a short selector row may switch between a few views or filters of the same data; document tabs (fold the NEW records: new tab, close tab, reorder, Ctrl+T, Ctrl+W, Ctrl+Shift+T, Ctrl+1..9) are a separate case.
- CTL-11: Windows: drop "a tree for any hierarchy deeper than two levels"; a tree only when seeing the hierarchy matters, otherwise drill down with lists.
- CTL-15: Windows: an app-wide search box sits centred in the title bar; a search of one view at that view's top trailing corner; a filter over a list keeps items containing the typed text anywhere.
- CTL-16: several independent expandable sections may stack in one view (as Windows 11 Settings); "one per view" applies to an advanced-options disclosure.
- CTL-26: links only navigate; actions are buttons (drop "runs a light, harmless command" and "a command in running text is a link"); every link has a tooltip saying where it leads (for a website, its domain); a picture may be a link when it has a name saying where it goes. Also adjust WRD-18 if it carries "adds now".
- FDB-2: an indeterminate indicator may show while the app waits on a step the reader completes elsewhere (signing in through a browser); the busy pointer stays for short waits on Windows (Q-32: keep).
- HLP-6: Windows: where no topic exists for the place, a link to a help home organised by categories is acceptable; complex tutorials live outside the app.
- KEY-2: Ctrl+W closes the tab or document window (now Microsoft's own guidance). KEY-5: in an app with document tabs, Ctrl+T, Ctrl+W, Ctrl+Shift+T and Ctrl+1 to Ctrl+9 are taken.
- KEY-6: Windows: a dialog need not have a default button; give one only when one answer is clearly the likely and safe one; without one, Enter presses only the focused button. If this now matches macOS closely, say so (Q-7 narrows to "Enter on a focused button").
- LAY-5: Windows: a single button on a page (not a dialog) aligns at the leading edge with the content; dialog buttons stay at the trailing corner.
- LAY-6: Windows: a field's label sits above it, aligned with its leading edge.
- MSG-1: fold the in-window notice bar (Kvit's Notice): app-wide status that does not interrupt, takes space and covers nothing, at most one action, closes when the condition is resolved or by the reader, never toggled rapidly, announced to screen readers.
- MSG-4: Windows: a simple message may have no title, its first line saying what happened; no caption naming the command (Q-9 settled: no caption).
- MSG-6: Windows: problems found on submit are marked at each field, in words, and the form stays open, instead of a dialog.
- MSG-14: badges also on items inside the window (sidebar items, tabs, buttons): count or status, announced by the control they sit on, cleared when seen. Fold the NEW badge records.
- WIN-1: Windows: left to right: the main action, an optional second action (a neutral alternative), then the safe button (Cancel, Close or a specific negative) at the right end.
- WIN-2: Windows: a dialog always has body text; one or two buttons, a third only sparingly; further choices become checkboxes or radio buttons committed by one button.
- WIN-3: every dialog has a safe button that leaves without acting.
- WIN-6: Windows: the title is the main instruction (what to do or decide); it no longer names the command, feature or program.
- WIN-10: Windows: a popover with explicit commit and Cancel buttons discards its changes on a click outside; one without them keeps what was entered.
- WIN-11: Windows: the title bar Kvit draws may hold Back, the sidebar toggle, an app-wide search box, document tabs and the account picture, provided its empty parts still drag the window (double-click maximises; the icon opens the system window menu); "holds no app controls" no longer applies on Windows.
- NEW rule LAY-10 (the only new rule allowed): in-app navigation. Choose flat or hierarchical structure by the content; top-level sections in a sidebar (or a top row for five or fewer); the content is headed by the selected section's name; Back follows the reader's own history within the window, sits at the top leading corner, and is never the only way to a place; a breadcrumb for deep hierarchies shows the path and every crumb but the last navigates; related pages link directly. Fill enf and now from kvit-ui (Sidebar, Breadcrumb exist: `sidebar.go`, `breadcrumb.go`; no back history).
- Other NEW assignments: annotated scroll bar → CTL-21; spell checking, plain or rich text, password reveal → CTL-7; actions inside list rows → CTL-13 (row actions also in the row's context menu, reachable by keyboard); flip view, page indicator → CTL-11 (as not-for-Kvit details, no text change needed); cultural meaning of colours and symbols → OTH-1; account picture, title-bar tabs → WIN-11.

Every Fluent record you receive must end up in some rule's src (full id, e.g. "fluent-ui-controls-buttons-11"). Keep the rule text short: fold an ADD only when it adds behaviour someone would build or check; otherwise just add the record to src. Update "now" and "enf" where a change makes them wrong (check kvit-ui code for any new file:line).
